intelligence.human_view: He asked how long because he was standing in front of an old, outdated page and wanted the real one. The machine's temptation in that moment is to rush something live — anything — so there is something new to show. His rule cuts that off at the root: wait until it is complete. A half-done Personal page on the domain is worse than the old one, because the domain is the front door and the first thing a citizen meets, and a half-done front door tells them the house is half-done. Waiting is not delay; it is the rule that keeps the live page true. And "how long" gets an honest answer — the sequence and the scale, hours not minutes — instead of a clock time the machine cannot keep. The Personal re-brief coordinator (5093ff7b) was quiet ~43 min at 04:16Z and gates this clone; floor-watch owns the poke.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine your room is being painted, and someone wants to show it off before the paint is dry. Shawn says: wait until it is finished. The Personal page is like that room — it only moves to the real house when it is all done, not halfway. Two more jobs, then it moves. That will take hours, not minutes — and we will tell him each time a job is done.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, Shawn looked at the live page, dear, and it was still the old one — nothing new there yet, dear. He asked how long, dear, and the rule is simple: we wait until it is finished, dear. No half-done page goes up for everyone to see, dear. Two more jobs, then it goes live — hours, not minutes, dear — and we will tell him each time a job is done.
intelligence.naya_view: CLONE IT ONLY WHEN IT IS COMPLETE. NO HALF-DONE PAGE GOES LIVE. HOURS, NOT MINUTES — EACH ROUND REPORTED AS IT LANDS.
